'Split line with an inspection: the moved note offers Build lines

'When a work order line that carries a completed inspection is split onto a new work order, its inspection report note moves to the new work order. After that: (1) Should the moved note offer Build lines, when the inspection has a Monitor or Not OK finding and has not been built from? (2) Should View PDF and Download on the moved note open and download the report? (3) Should the asset's Inspections tab show the new work order in the inspection's Work order column and link to it? In short: after a split, which work order counts as the one the inspection was run on?

'PRD v43 S7-E4 (6 Oct): "The inspection's report notes are not records of the build: when a line with an inspection is split onto a new work order, those notes move with the line and are removed from the original. Work orders split before this rule keep their notes where they are." Milos Vasic on SV-10913 (6 Oct) confirmed only that the notes move with the line and are removed from the old work order. Build lines on the moved note, working View PDF/Download and the asset row linking to the new work order come from Viktoria Videnovic's proposal (items 3-4) and Stefan Vukovic's (developer) ready-for-QA notes of 7 Oct; the PM did not answer those points. The note move itself is already covered by the planned update of C88540 and is not repeated here. Partly arguable from S4-R1 and S5-R21, but neither says which work order the inspection was 'run on' after a split.

'S7-E4: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)
SV-10913: 6 Oct 2026 (Milos Vasic (PM) in Jira - notes move, removed from the old work order)
SV-10913: 7 Oct 2026 (Stefan Vukovic (developer) in Jira - Build lines shown, View PDF/Download work, asset row links to the new work order)

'Phone Save & exit: unsaved answers, the prompt and closed work orders

'You agreed on 9 Oct that the phone gets Save & exit like the desktop. Please confirm three details the developer built: (1) On a phone, are answers that were not saved (by Save & exit, the 'Unsaved changes' prompt's Save, or Submit) lost when the phone locks or the page reloads? (2) Does Save & exit take the technician back to the work order without showing the 'Unsaved changes' prompt? (3) On a completed or invoiced work order, is there no ⋮ menu and so no Save & exit?

'PRD v43 and the 22 Sep spec are silent on saving while filling (V1 relied on a Save button; no auto-save). Milos Vasic, SV-10938, 9 Oct: "if we can improve this to work similar as desktop ( save and exit ) that can be great". Stefan Vukovic (developer), SV-10938, 9 Oct: "tap Save & exit: you land on the work order with no 'Unsaved changes' prompt"; "Answer the other field and lock the phone, or reload the page, without pressing Save & exit: that answer is not kept. Answers are still saved only by Save & exit, the 'Unsaved changes' prompt's Save, or Submit"; "On a completed or invoiced work order, the ⋮ menu isn't shown, so there is no Save & exit." A case that expects answers to be lost must not ship on a developer's statement.

'SV-10938: 9 Oct 2026 (Milos Vasic (PM) in Jira - Save & exit like the desktop)
SV-10938: 9 Oct 2026 (Stefan Vukovic (developer) in Jira - the three details above)

'An inspection on a completed line can still be submitted

'Since 9 Oct the build lets an inspection on a completed work order line be filled in, submitted and its report generated without uncompleting the line. Before, it was read-only with the message 'Inspection is in read only mode. Uncomplete the line to submit it.' Is this change wanted? If yes, please also confirm: adding a new inspection to a completed line is still refused, and an inspection on a declined line, or on a completed or invoiced work order, stays read-only.

'PRD v43 and the 22 Sep spec say nothing about it. Stefan Vukovic (developer), SV-10937, 9 Oct: "An inspection on a completed line can now be filled in and submitted, and its report generated, without uncompleting the line"; unchanged by design: "Adding a new inspection to a completed line is still refused" and "A declined line, or a completed or invoiced work order, still makes the inspection read-only". QA pass by Mudassir Qamar, 12 Oct. No product statement on the ticket. It reverses existing behaviour, so it needs a product decision; your 'lets disregard this one for now' on SV-8128 (9 Oct) was about tying line completion to inspection state and is not a sign-off for this.
'SV-10937: 9 Oct 2026 (Stefan Vukovic (developer) in Jira; QA pass Mudassir Qamar 2026-10-12; no PM statement)
'With many findings, each proposed line lists the findings it covers

'May one proposed line cover several findings (listing each finding it covers), and may the system itself add a plain line for a finding ShopCoach leaves out? The specification currently says each proposed line names the finding it came from, and that no empty lines are created because there is no non-AI line builder.

'PRD v43 S15-R13: "Each proposed line will name the finding it came from"; S15-R21: "Each proposed line will carry the identifier of the finding it came from"; Key Decision: "No empty lines are created. There is no non-AI line builder to fall back to." S15-R14 / S2-E3 (every flagged finding represented by at least one line; a large set is split, not dropped) are unchanged since 22 Sep and already covered by C88518 and C88544. Only the developer states the new behaviour: Stefan Vukovic, SV-10910, 7 Oct: "When ShopCoach leaves a finding out, it retries that finding, and then our backend adds a plain line for any finding still uncovered. A single line may cover more than one finding when one job on the same component fixes them all." SV-10910 is Blocked; SOURCE-CHECK L18 already logs this as a PO question.
'SV-10910: 7 Oct 2026 (Stefan Vukovic (developer) in Jira)

'Each per-axle field starts with its own axles, set to Dual

'Two points the specification does not cover: (1) When a template has two per-axle fields, does each field keep its own axles, so adding an axle or switching Single/Dual on one field does not change the other? (2) When an inspection starts, are the starting axles set to Dual, with Drum or Disc not chosen?

'PRD v43 and the 22 Sep spec are silent on both. The technical plan (Dusan Radulovic, revision of 23 Sep, copy received 30 Sep) says each per-axle field keeps its own axle list and that the starting axles are seeded Dual with brake type blank; the plan itself marks the Dual start 'confirm at Phase 5 build'. The design's untouched axle is drawn as Dual (supports, does not decide), and a QA defect description (SV-10877, 5 Oct) mentions 'Axle 1, which is Dual by default' as an observation of the build, not a decision. The tech plan informs but never overrules. Not part of the question: the starting axle count is already a spec rule since 22 Sep (S8-R9, S12-R29; covered by C88550 and C88569), and 'no values or verdicts filled in' is covered by C154647.

'Tech plan: axle list per per-axle field: 23 Sep 2026 (Dusan Radulovic in the technical plan (copy received 30 Sep 2026))
Tech plan: starting axles seeded Dual: 23 Sep 2026 (Dusan Radulovic in the technical plan (copy received 30 Sep 2026); marked 'confirm at Phase 5 build')
